prompt: We're adding a generic webhook handler to support customers who use custom providers beyond GitHub and Stripe. The PR is up at pr/352/. I need a security review focused on the new generic handler - signature verification, replay protection, and callback safety are my main concerns given this will handle customer data. Look at how it compares to our existing GitHub and Stripe handlers for consistency. Write your review to REVIEW.md at the top of the project. End it with a fenced json list of findings, each with location (path/to/file.ext:LINE, with line numbers of the file as it is in the project), severity (critical, high, medium, low or nit), issue and fix.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const S=["critical","high","medium","low","nit"];process.exit(L.every(x=>x.location&&S.includes(String(x.severity).toLowerCase())&&(x.issue||x.fix||x.text))?0:1)'

node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);let n=0;for(const x of L)for(const m of String(x.location).matchAll(/([A-Za-z0-9_.\/-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+):(\d+)/g)){n++;let c;try{c=fs.readFileSync(m[1],"utf8").split("\n").length}catch{process.exit(1)}if(+m[2]<1||+m[2]>c)process.exit(1)}process.exit(n?0:1)'

rubric.criterion: Each important finding explains the concrete consequence in this project and suggests a fix a developer can act on, without inventing problems that don't exist (code cannot check this because it requires understanding the actual security impact in context).

findingsKey.finding: Signature verification uses re-serialized parsed JSON instead of the raw request body, which can cause verification failures if the client signed a different JSON serialization.
Signature comparison uses plain string equality (===) which is vulnerable to timing attacks that could leak the expected signature.
Delivery ID tracking has no time window - IDs are stored indefinitely in memory, violating the replay protection requirement in docs/security.md for a configured window.
The handler ignores the X-Timestamp header and never validates timestamp age, allowing replay attacks beyond the 5-minute window specified in docs/provider-spec.md.
WEBHOOK_SECRET falls back to a hard-coded default when the environment variable is missing, which would use the same weak secret in production if misconfigured.
The debug log prints the signature header which contains the HMAC, potentially leaking it in logs if LOG_LEVEL=debug is enabled in production.
The server startup log prints whether the webhook secret is configured, which could indicate to an attacker whether the default secret is being used.
